newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Leibler sees float of Australia's TEN network.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Leibler sees float of Australia's TEN network.

text.p: Businessman Isi Leibler said on Monday that TEN Group Ltd would eventually be listed on the stock exchange, but this may not be finalised at a meeting of directors next month.
Leilber last Friday acquired the 10 percent voting stake in Australia's third-ranked television network for A$59.15 million, or A$13 per share, from Singleton Group Ltd.
"I believe there is going to be a float," he told Reuters.
"That is what our utlimate interest would be because I think that is how we are going to maximise the greatest potential of the price."
"We are still going to be looking at a potential listing, and evaluating all sorts of opportunities," he said.
Leibler now has a 15 percent voting stake in TEN and a 7.5 percent economic interest.

He would not comment when asked if the purchase of the Singleton stake had been financed by Selli Pty Ltd, a company described in last Friday's statement by Singleton as an nominee company of CanWest Global Communications Corp.
Corporate sources involved in the transaction earlier told Reuters that Selli had provided the financing. CanWest has a 15 percent voting and a 57.5 percent economic interest in TEN.
Leibler, one of the founding shareholders in TEN when it came out of receivership in late 1992, said there was a very loose relationship between Selli and Canwest.
He said Selli was also associated with his company Leibler Media Holdings Pty Ltd.
The December board meeting of TEN would discuss the listing plans, but a timetable for the float still had not been set.
"It (a 1996 float) is going to be hard but nothing is impossible," Leibler said.
Singleton's sale was largely based on the company's frustration in reaching shareholder agreement on a listing.
"I am more patient than he (Singleton founder and TEN director John Singleton) is," said Leibler, who also agreed that he may eventually sell his own increased holding.
"I may be a seller but I must say I am very excited with the company and I would like to stay associated. Even if I sold, I would like to keep something in."
When the shareholders joined forces in 1992 they agreed to float TEN as soon as possible but this has been delayed by a boardroom dispute over potential tax liabilites from a listing.
Another sticking point has been the reluctance of CanWest to reduce its economic interest in a float.
The TEN network is valued at A$1.18 billion based on the Singleton sale price of A$13 per share. Singleton's economic interest was five percent.

A number of brokers have presented listing proposals which mostly revolve around a trust concept that would give some of the smaller shareholders a chance to realise their profits as well as easing the tax burden.
Other small investors such as Jack Cowin and Robert Whyte are keen to see TEN list, while the Australian Broadcasting Authority has recently asked TEN how the plans are progressing.
